The sanity script resolves the submission relative to its own parent directory. So running a copy from /workspace/tmp makes it look for /workspace/tmp/submission. Let me place the copy in a directory whose parent contains submission: e.g. /workspace/tt/sanity2.py with /workspace/tt/submission → but submission is at /app/submission which is /workspace/submission (since /app → /workspace).

So /app/public/sanity.py → parents[1] = /app = /workspace, and /workspace/submission = /app/submission. Right.

So to run a modified sanity, put it in /workspace/tmp/ and it looks for /workspace/tmp/submission. I could symlink... but symlinks in the submission are disallowed; elsewhere it's fine for testing. Actually simpler: just create /workspace/tmp/submission as a symlink to /app/submission for testing.

Actually, let me instead directly patch the sanity copy to point at the right submission path via --submission.

But first, the original sanity run failed at the suffix assert. Let me use --submission /app/submission and add the debug print.

arguments.command: cd /workspace/tmp/t1 && sed 's/assert suffix == expected\[2:\], "Example suffix mismatch"/assert suffix == expected[2:], "GOT %r EXP %r" % (suffix, expected[2:])/' /app/public/sanity.py > sanity2.py && python3 sanity2.py --submission /app/submission 2>&1 | head -30
